definition: to influence someone's opinion; or to move slowly from side to side

examples.text: The pamphlet swayed public opinion against the tax.
Tall buildings are designed to sway a little in strong wind.
A free dessert will not sway my review, but I appreciate the effort.

confused.note: To sway is to influence or to rock; to swat is to hit sharply.

questions.passage: The lawyer knew that facts alone would not ______ the jury. She closed her argument with the story of the victim's last morning, told so simply that several jurors wept.
questions.explanation: Moving the jurors with a story is influencing their opinion.

distractors.why: Omit means to leave out, which does not fit.
Confine means to restrict, which does not fit.
Spawn means to produce or give rise to, which does not fit a jury.

definition: to arrange things in a straight line; or to support or agree with a person, group, or idea

examples.text: The mirrors must be aligned to within a hair's width.
The small kingdom aligned itself with the stronger of its neighbors.
I aligned the picture frames along the hallway with a ruler.

confused.note: To align is to line up or side with; to allay is to calm a fear.

questions.passage: In the debate over the new dam, the fishing villages ______ themselves with the farmers. Both groups feared that the reservoir would flood their land, and together they sent a single delegation to the capital.
questions.explanation: Joining with the farmers in a shared position is siding with them.

distractors.why: Confided means told a secret to, which does not fit.
Degraded means lowered in quality or dignity, which does not fit.
Provoked means stirred up or angered, which does not fit joining forces.

partsNote: from Latin linea, "line": to bring to a line

definition: the quality of being real or true

examples.text: Experts confirmed the authenticity of the signature on the treaty.
Readers praised the authenticity of the novel's dialect.
I doubted the authenticity of a "designer" bag sold for ten dollars.

confused.note: Authenticity is genuineness; authority is the power to command.

questions.passage: The museum would not buy the painting until its ______ had been established. Laboratory tests of the canvas and pigments, together with a record of every previous owner, finally proved that it was genuine.
questions.explanation: Proving a painting is genuine establishes that it is real.

distractors.why: Disposition is a person's temperament, which does not fit.
An inversion is a reversal, which does not fit.
A synopsis is a summary, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Greek authentes, "one who acts on his own authority"

definition: having practical knowledge and good judgment

examples.text: The savvy merchant sold her ships a month before the war began.
A savvy researcher checks who paid for a study before trusting it.
My savvy cousin always knows which gas station is cheapest.

confused.note: Savvy means practically shrewd; to savor is to enjoy slowly.

questions.passage: First-time buyers are often dazzled by a low monthly payment. More ______ customers ask what the total cost will be once interest and fees are added.
questions.explanation: Asking about the true total cost shows practical good judgment.

distractors.why: Deficient means lacking, the opposite of being well informed.
Coarse means rough or crude, which does not fit.
Unilateral means done by one side alone, which does not fit.

definition: to officially accuse someone of a crime and try to prove it in court

examples.text: The crown prosecuted the printers for publishing the pamphlet.
The young lawyer must prosecute his own former teacher.
The sign warns that shoplifters will be prosecuted.

confused.note: To prosecute is to bring a legal case against; to persecute is to treat cruelly.

questions.passage: The government announced that it would ______ the company's former executives. They are accused of hiding the firm's losses from investors and will stand trial in the spring.
questions.explanation: Bringing accused executives to trial is charging them in court.

distractors.why: Persecute means to treat cruelly over time; a court case is prosecution.
Confide means to tell a secret, which does not fit.
Overlook means to ignore or excuse, the opposite of bringing charges.

definition: to fail to notice something; or to choose to ignore a mistake or fault

examples.text: The first team overlooked a faint signal that the second team caught.
The inspectors overlooked the cracked beam that later gave way.
I will overlook the fact that you ate my leftovers, this once.

confused.note: To overlook is to miss or excuse; to oversee is to supervise.

questions.passage: Proofreaders caught hundreds of small errors in the manuscript. They ______ the largest one, however: the hero's name was spelled two different ways on the cover itself.
questions.explanation: Failing to notice the error on the cover is missing it.

distractors.why: Contemplated means thought deeply about, which they did not do.
Provoked means caused or angered, which does not fit.
Accrued means accumulated, which does not fit.

definition: to cause a strong reaction, especially anger; to deliberately annoy

examples.text: The new tax provoked riots in three cities.
The injection may provoke a mild fever.
My brother pokes me just to provoke a reaction.

confused.note: To provoke is to stir up; to revoke is to cancel.

questions.passage: The minister's remark was not meant to cause trouble. It nonetheless ______ an angry response from teachers, thousands of whom marched on the capital the following week.
questions.explanation: The remark caused a strong, angry reaction.

distractors.why: Confined means restricted, which does not fit.
Degraded means lowered in quality, which does not fit.
Overlooked means failed to notice, which does not fit.

definition: a person's usual mood or way of behaving; a tendency

examples.text: The heroine's sunny disposition survives every misfortune the author throws at her.
Some breeds have a calmer disposition than others.
My dog has the disposition of a much smaller, more nervous animal.

confused.note: A disposition is a temperament; a deposition is sworn testimony or the removal of a ruler.

questions.passage: Though raised in the same house, the two brothers differed greatly in ______. One was cheerful, talkative, and quick to forgive; the other brooded for days over the smallest slight.
questions.explanation: Being cheerful or brooding by nature is a matter of temperament.

distractors.why: Lineage is ancestry, which brothers share.
Authenticity is genuineness, which does not fit.
A synopsis is a summary, which does not fit.

definition: relating to the quality or character of something, not to its amount

examples.text: Interviews gave the study qualitative depth that numbers could not.
There was a qualitative difference between the two armies: one was trained, the other was not.
The reviews gave a qualitative sense of the hotel that star ratings missed.

confused.note: Qualitative concerns what kind; quantitative concerns how much.

questions.passage: The survey's numbers showed that patients were dissatisfied but not why. For that the researchers turned to ______ methods, sitting with twenty patients for an hour each and recording what they said.
questions.explanation: Long interviews describe the character of an experience, not its amount.

distractors.why: Quantitative means numerical, which is what the survey already provided.
Unilateral means one-sided, which does not fit.
Malignant means harmful, which does not fit.

definition: rough in texture; or rude and offensive

examples.text: Coarse sand lets water drain faster than fine clay.
The sailor's coarse jokes scandalize the vicar's wife.
The towel was so coarse it felt like sandpaper.

confused.note: Coarse means rough or crude; a course is a path, a class, or part of a meal.

questions.passage: The cloth worn by the peasants was ______, woven from thick, uneven thread that scratched the skin. Only the wealthy could afford the smooth linen sold in the city.
questions.explanation: Thick thread that scratches makes a rough cloth.

distractors.why: Supple means soft and flexible, the opposite of scratchy cloth.
Equitable means fair, which does not fit.
Emphatic means forceful in expression, which does not fit.

definition: to think about something seriously for a long time; to consider doing something

examples.text: The old captain contemplates the sea he will not sail again.
The king contemplated abdication for a year before acting.
I contemplated a second slice of cake and then stopped pretending I had a choice.

confused.note: To contemplate is to think deeply; to complement is to complete.

questions.passage: The offer was generous, but she did not accept at once. She took a week to ______ it, walking each evening along the river and weighing what she would gain against what she would leave behind.
questions.explanation: Weighing the offer over a week is thinking about it seriously.

distractors.why: Omit means to leave out, which does not fit.
Expend means to use up, which does not fit.
Prosecute means to bring to trial, which does not fit.

definition: to cause something to develop or be produced, often in large numbers

The invention of the press spawned a thousand pamphlets.
One viral video spawned a whole week of copycats at our school.

confused.note: To spawn is to give rise to; to span is to stretch across.

questions.passage: The success of the first detective novel ______ countless imitations. Within a decade, hundreds of fictional investigators, each with a loyal assistant and an odd habit, crowded the shelves.
questions.explanation: The novel gave rise to many imitations.

distractors.why: Confined means restricted, the opposite of producing many.
Omitted means left out, which does not fit.
Aligned means lined up or sided with, which does not fit.

definition: a short summary of a book, play, or report

examples.text: The back cover gives a synopsis that spoils the ending.
Each paper begins with a synopsis of its methods and findings.
Give me a synopsis of the meeting; I do not need all ninety minutes.

confused.note: A synopsis is a summary; a synapse is a junction between nerve cells.

questions.passage: Committee members had no time to read the full four-hundred-page report. Each was given a two-page ______ that listed its main findings and its seven recommendations.
questions.explanation: Two pages listing the main findings is a short summary.

distractors.why: A corollary is a natural consequence, which does not fit.
An inversion is a reversal, which does not fit.
Lineage is ancestry, which does not fit.

definition: fair and reasonable; treating everyone equally

The committee sought an equitable way to share telescope time.
We found an equitable solution: whoever cuts the cake picks last.

confused.note: Equitable means fair; equivocal means unclear or evasive.

questions.passage: The three heirs agreed that the estate should be divided in an ______ manner. Each received land of the same value, and the one who took the house paid the other two a share of its worth.
questions.explanation: Giving each heir the same value is fair to all.

distractors.why: Unilateral means decided by one side alone, but all three agreed.
Deficient means lacking, which does not fit.
Coarse means rough or crude, which does not fit.

definition: done by one person, group, or country without the agreement of others

The lab made a unilateral change to the protocol without telling its partners.
My roommate made a unilateral decision to repaint the kitchen orange.

confused.note: Unilateral means done by one side; universal means applying to all.

questions.passage: The agreement required that any change to the border be approved by both governments. One country's ______ decision to build a wall along the river was therefore a clear violation.
questions.explanation: A decision made by one country without the other is one-sided.

distractors.why: Equitable means fair, which a violation is not.
Emphatic means forceful, which is not the point.
Qualitative means relating to character or kind, which does not fit.

definition: not having enough of something; not good enough

The army was deficient in cannon and relied on speed.
My diet this week has been deficient in anything green.

confused.note: Deficient means lacking enough of something; defective means having a flaw.

questions.passage: Sailors on long voyages once suffered from a disease that made their gums bleed. Doctors eventually learned that their diet was ______ in vitamin C, and a daily ration of lemon juice ended the problem.
questions.explanation: A diet without enough vitamin C is lacking in it.

distractors.why: Supple means flexible, which does not fit.

Emphatic means forceful, which does not fit.

A malignant rumor spread through the school by lunchtime.

confused.note: Malignant is an adjective meaning very harmful; to malign is to speak ill of.

questions.passage: The surgeon removed the lump and sent it to the laboratory. The patient waited anxiously to learn whether it was harmless or ______, since the answer would determine whether further treatment was needed.
questions.explanation: The contrast with "harmless" calls for a word meaning dangerous and likely to spread.

distractors.why: Equitable means fair, which does not fit.
Supple means flexible, which does not fit.
Qualitative means relating to kind, which does not fit.

examples.text: The entrenched nobility blocked every reform for a century.

My family's entrenched habit of eating in front of the television survived three new rules.

confused.note: Entrenched means firmly fixed; enchanted means delighted or under a spell.

questions.passage: The custom of closing every shop for three hours at midday is deeply ______ in the town. Mayors have tried to end it four times in fifty years, and each time shopkeepers have simply ignored the new rules.
questions.explanation: A custom that survives every attempt to end it is firmly established.

distractors.why: Deficient means lacking, which does not fit.
Unilateral means one-sided, which does not fit.
Coarse means rough, which does not fit.

definition: to lower the quality of something; to treat someone without respect

Copying the photo ten times degraded it into a gray smear.

confused.note: To degrade is to lower in quality or dignity; to downgrade is to lower in rank or rating.

questions.passage: Ecologists warn that heavy grazing will ______ the grassland. Once the plant cover is thin, rain washes the soil away, and land that fed thousands of animals can turn to bare rock within a generation.
questions.explanation: Losing plants and soil lowers the quality of the land.

distractors.why: Contemplate means to think about, which does not fit.
Align means to line up, which does not fit.
Accrue means to accumulate, which does not fit.

definition: a change in which something becomes the opposite of what it was; a reversal of the normal order

examples.text: A temperature inversion trapped the smoke in the valley.
The play's joke is an inversion: the servants give orders and the masters obey.
Breakfast for dinner is my favorite inversion.

confused.note: An inversion is a reversal; an invasion is an entry by force.

questions.passage: The festival is built on an ______ of everyday roles. For one day each year, children run the town council, teachers sit at the pupils' desks, and the mayor sweeps the square.
questions.explanation: Children governing and the mayor sweeping reverse the normal order.

distractors.why: A synopsis is a summary, which does not fit.
A disposition is a temperament, which does not fit.
A corollary is a consequence, which does not fit.

definition: said or done with force, leaving no doubt

examples.text: The assembly's emphatic rejection of the treaty ended the talks.

My mom's answer to "Can I skip school?" was an emphatic no.

confused.note: Emphatic means forceful; empathic means showing empathy.

questions.passage: Asked whether the bridge was safe, the engineer gave an ______ answer. "Absolutely not," she said. "I would not let my worst enemy drive across it, and I have told the mayor so in writing three times."
questions.explanation: "Absolutely not," repeated in writing, is forceful and leaves no doubt.

distractors.why: Deficient means lacking, which does not fit.
Equitable means fair, which does not fit.
Supple means flexible, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Greek phainein, "to show": showing in

definition: to leave something out, either deliberately or by mistake

examples.text: The official history omits any mention of the defeat.

I omitted the part about the dent when I told Dad about my day.

confused.note: To omit is to leave out; to emit is to give off.

questions.passage: The published version of the diary is not complete. Its editors chose to ______ several entries in which the author criticized people who were still living when the book appeared.
questions.explanation: Leaving entries out of the book is omitting them.

distractors.why: Spawn means to produce, which does not fit.
Sway means to influence, which does not fit.
Provoke means to stir up, which does not fit.

A sprained ankle confined me to the couch for a week.

questions.passage: The speaker was asked to ______ her remarks to ten minutes. With six others waiting to address the committee, the chair explained, there would be no time for anything longer.
questions.explanation: Keeping remarks within ten minutes is restricting them.

distractors.why: Confide means to tell a secret; it looks similar but does not mean restrict.
Accrue means to accumulate, which does not fit.
Degrade means to lower in quality, which does not fit.

definition: to increase in amount over time; to come as a natural result

examples.text: Small errors accrue until the model's predictions are useless.
Great power accrued to whoever controlled the river crossing.
Interest accrues on the savings account every month.

confused.note: To accrue is to accumulate; to accuse is to charge with wrongdoing.

questions.passage: The loan seemed small when she signed for it. But interest continued to ______ during the four years she spent at university, and by graduation she owed nearly twice the original sum.
questions.explanation: Interest building up over four years is accumulating.

distractors.why: Confide means to tell a secret, which does not fit.
Omit means to leave out, which does not fit.
Sway means to influence, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin crescere, "to grow": to grow toward

examples.text: The heroine confides her fears to the old gardener.
The king confided his plan to only two ministers.
I confided in my sister that I had not actually read the book.

confused.note: To confide is to share a secret; to confine is to restrict.

questions.passage: The young scientist had told no one of her doubts about the experiment. At last she ______ in a senior colleague, who listened in silence and then admitted that he had been worried about the same results for months.
questions.explanation: Telling a trusted colleague her private doubts is sharing a secret.

distractors.why: Confined means restricted; it resembles the right word but means something else.

Prosecuted means brought to trial, which does not fit.

I expended most of my allowance on a single concert ticket.

confused.note: To expend is to use up; to expand is to grow larger.

questions.passage: The committee ______ a great deal of effort on a question that turned out not to matter. After six months of meetings it learned that the land in dispute had been sold a year earlier.
questions.explanation: Six months of meetings is effort used up.

distractors.why: Stipulated means demanded as a condition, which does not fit.

Thrived means flourished, which does not fit.

partsNote: to weigh out, to pay out

definition: tending to examine your own thoughts and feelings

In exile the general grew introspective and wrote his memoirs.
Long bus rides make me introspective.

questions.passage: As a young man the poet wrote about battles and kings. His late work is more ______, turning from public events to his own doubts, memories, and fear of growing old.

distractors.why: Omnipresent means present everywhere, which does not fit.

definition: bending and moving easily; flexible

A few weeks of stretching made my hamstrings supple again.

confused.note: Supple means flexible; subtle means not obvious.

questions.passage: Leather that is left to dry becomes hard and cracks. Rubbed regularly with oil, it stays ______ and can be folded a thousand times without splitting.
questions.explanation: Leather that folds without splitting bends easily.

distractors.why: Paltry means small and worthless, which does not fit.
Unjust means unfair, which does not fit.
Integral means essential to the whole, which does not fit.

definition: present everywhere at the same time

Phones are omnipresent at concerts now, held up like tiny candles.

confused.note: Omnipresent means everywhere; omnipotent means all-powerful.

questions.passage: In the weeks before the election, the candidate's face was ______. It looked down from billboards, flickered on every screen, and was printed on paper cups handed out at train stations.
questions.explanation: A face on billboards, screens, and cups is everywhere at once.

distractors.why: Introspective means inward-looking, which does not fit.
Untoward means unexpected and inconvenient, which does not fit.

examples.text: The treaty stipulated that the fort be torn down within a year.

The lease stipulates no pets, which my landlord has not noticed I ignore.

questions.passage: The will did not leave the house to the nephew outright. It ______ that he could inherit only if he lived in it for ten years and kept the garden exactly as his aunt had planted it.
questions.explanation: Setting conditions for inheriting is stating clearly what must be done.

distractors.why: Expended means used up, which does not fit.
Thrived means flourished, which does not fit.
Dismayed means distressed, which does not fit.

Nothing untoward happened at the party, unless you count the cake.

questions.passage: Organizers had feared trouble at the match between the two rival clubs. In the event nothing ______ occurred: supporters sang, the game ended in a draw, and the crowd went home peacefully.

distractors.why: Integral means essential, which does not fit.
Lenient means not strict, which does not fit.
Systematic means methodical, which does not fit.

examples.text: The duke traced his lineage to the first kings of the island.
Genetic tests showed that the two populations share a lineage.
My dog's lineage is a mystery involving at least four breeds.

confused.note: Lineage is ancestry; linkage is a connection.

questions.passage: The horse's value lay partly in its ______. Its mother and grandfather had both won the national championship, and breeders could trace its ancestors back for eleven generations.
questions.explanation: Champion parents and traced ancestors make up a line of descent.

distractors.why: Clout is influence, which does not fit.
Mirth is laughter, which does not fit.
A corollary is a consequence, which does not fit.

It seemed unjust that my brother got dessert after I did all the dishes.

questions.passage: Critics called the law ______. It fined people for sleeping in public parks while doing nothing to provide them with any other place to go.

confused.note: Foreseeable means able to be predicted; foreseen means actually predicted.

questions.passage: The court ruled that the accident had been entirely ______. Inspectors had warned twice that the scaffold was unstable, and anyone who read their reports could have predicted its collapse.

distractors.why: Untoward means unfortunate; the ruling is about whether it could be predicted.
Paltry means small and worthless, which does not fit.
Integral means essential, which does not fit.

questions.passage: To the ______ of the museum's staff, the newly cleaned painting looked worse than before. The restorer had removed not only two centuries of dirt but also much of the original color.

As the only one with a car, my sister has considerable clout in our friend group.

questions.passage: The small farming party had only five seats in the assembly. It nonetheless had considerable ______, because neither of the two large parties could form a government without its support.
questions.explanation: Holding the deciding seats gives the party influence beyond its size.

distractors.why: Dismay is shock and disappointment, which does not fit.
Mirth is laughter, which does not fit.
Lineage is ancestry, which does not fit.

definition: very small in amount and so not worth much

examples.text: The veterans received a paltry pension of a few coins a month.
The expedition returned with a paltry three specimens.
I was offered a paltry five dollars for a bike worth fifty.

questions.passage: After a year of negotiation, the company offered its workers a ______ raise of one percent. Union leaders pointed out that prices had risen eight percent over the same period.

distractors.why: Lenient means not strict, which does not fit.

definition: something that follows naturally from something else

distractors.why: Clout is influence, which does not fit.
Lineage is ancestry, which does not fit.
Dismay is shock, which does not fit.

questions.passage: The defendant claimed that he had never been in the building. The prosecution answered with ______ evidence: a security recording that showed him entering the lobby and signing the visitors' book.

Lenient means not strict, which does not fit.

definition: happiness and laughter

examples.text: The hall rings with mirth when the jester trips over the dog.

questions.passage: The speaker had meant his remarks to be serious. His unfortunate habit of mispronouncing the mayor's name, however, caused such ______ in the audience that he had to stop twice to let the laughter die down.

distractors.why: Dismay is shock and worry, which does not match laughter.
Clout is influence, which does not fit.
A corollary is a consequence, which does not fit.

definition: not strict in punishing or controlling; merciful

examples.text: The new governor was lenient toward first offenders.

My grandparents are far more lenient about bedtime than my parents.

questions.passage: The judge was known for being ______ with young offenders. Where the law permitted a year in prison, she usually ordered a few months of community service and a letter of apology.

distractors.why: Unjust means unfair; the passage describes mercy, not unfairness.

Pivotal means crucial, which does not fit.

definition: to limit or soften a statement so that it is less general; or to meet the requirements for something

examples.text: The authors qualify their claim by noting that the sample was small.
Only landowners qualified to vote under the old law.
I should qualify what I said: the movie was good for a sequel.

confused.note: To qualify is to limit a claim or meet a standard; to quantify is to measure.

questions.passage: The scientist was careful to ______ her conclusion. The drug had worked, she said, but only in adults under sixty, and only when it was given within two days of the first symptoms.
questions.explanation: Adding conditions that limit the claim is qualifying it.

distractors.why: Expend means to use up, which does not fit.
Stipulate means to demand as a condition of an agreement; she is limiting her own claim.
Thrive means to flourish, which does not fit.

definition: necessary and important as a part of a whole

examples.text: The keel is integral to the ship's stability.
The river trade was integral to the city's wealth.
Garlic is integral to my grandmother's sauce; do not suggest leaving it out.

confused.note: Integral means essential to the whole; to integrate is to combine into a whole.

questions.passage: Music is not an optional extra at the school. It is ______ to the curriculum: every student learns an instrument, and mathematics lessons often begin with a discussion of rhythm.
questions.explanation: Something built into every part of the curriculum is essential to it.

distractors.why: Paltry means worthlessly small, which does not fit.
Untoward means unfortunate, which does not fit.
Foreseeable means predictable, which does not fit.

definition: done according to a careful plan and in a thorough way

examples.text: A systematic search of the genome took the team three years.
The census was the first systematic count of the kingdom's people.
I made a systematic search of the house and found my keys in the fridge.

confused.note: Systematic means methodical; systemic means affecting a whole system.

questions.passage: Earlier excavations at the site had been careless, with diggers simply collecting whatever looked valuable. The new team took a ______ approach, dividing the ground into numbered squares and recording the exact position of every object.
questions.explanation: Numbered squares and exact records are a careful, planned method.

distractors.why: Lenient means not strict, which does not fit.
Introspective means inward-looking, which does not fit.
Paltry means worthlessly small, which does not fit.

definition: not enough or not good enough for a purpose

examples.text: The sample was inadequate for a reliable test.
The city's walls proved inadequate against the new cannon.
One towel is inadequate for three people at the beach.

confused.note: Inadequate means not enough; inaccurate means not correct.

questions.passage: Engineers warned that the town's flood defenses were ______. The walls had been built to hold back a river two meters above its normal level, and in three of the last ten years it had risen higher than that.
questions.explanation: Walls lower than recent floods are not good enough.

distractors.why: Integral means essential, which is not the warning.
Irrefutable means impossible to disprove, which does not fit.
Supple means flexible, which does not fit.

definition: to grow, develop, or be successful

examples.text: The moss thrives in damp shade.
The port thrived for two centuries on the salt trade.
My sister thrives on deadlines; I crumble.

confused.note: To thrive is to flourish; thrift is careful use of money.

questions.passage: Few plants can survive on the windswept island. One species of grass, however, ______ there, covering whole hillsides and growing taller than it does anywhere on the mainland.
questions.explanation: Covering hillsides and growing tall is flourishing.

distractors.why: Stipulates means requires as a condition, which does not fit.
Expends means uses up, which does not fit.
Qualifies means meets a requirement or limits a claim, which does not fit.

definition: of crucial importance to how something develops

examples.text: The battle at the bridge was the pivotal moment of the war.
The 1953 paper played a pivotal role in the new science of genetics.
The pivotal moment of the game was a penalty kick in the last minute.

confused.note: Pivotal is the adjective; a pivot is the point on which something turns.

questions.passage: Historians regard the invention of the printing press as a ______ event. Before it, books were copied by hand and owned by a few; within fifty years, millions of printed volumes had spread new ideas across a continent.
questions.explanation: An invention on which the spread of ideas turned is of crucial importance.

distractors.why: Paltry means worthlessly small, the opposite of a turning point.
Untoward means unfortunate, which does not fit.
Foreseeable means predictable, which is not what the examples show.

partsNote: from "pivot," the point on which something turns

definition: careful not to attract attention or reveal private information

examples.text: The envoy made discreet inquiries about the king's health.
A discreet cough from the butler warns that someone is at the door.
I gave my friend a discreet nudge when the teacher looked our way.

confused.note: Discreet means tactful and careful; discrete means separate and distinct.

questions.passage: The hotel's staff are trained to be ______. They never mention a guest's name in the lobby, do not discuss who is staying on which floor, and are said to have kept the visits of three presidents entirely secret.
questions.explanation: Never revealing who is staying shows care not to disclose private information.

distractors.why: Omnipresent means present everywhere, which does not fit.
Unjust means unfair, which does not fit.
Inadequate means not good enough, which does not fit.

definition: so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering

examples.text: The difference between the two measurements was negligible.
The tax raised a negligible sum and cost the king his popularity.
The chance of rain was negligible, so of course it poured.

confused.note: Negligible means too small to matter; negligent means careless.

questions.passage: The new fuel is slightly cheaper to produce, but the saving is ______. Spread across a year of driving, it amounts to less than the price of a single cup of coffee.
questions.explanation: A yearly saving smaller than a coffee is too small to matter.

distractors.why: Pivotal means crucial, the opposite of a tiny saving.
Irrefutable means impossible to disprove, which does not fit.
Integral means essential, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin neglegere, "to disregard": able to be ignored

definition: so important or useful that it is impossible to manage without

examples.text: Water is indispensable to every known form of life.
The interpreter proved indispensable to the expedition.
A good raincoat is indispensable in this town.

confused.note: Indispensable means absolutely necessary; indisputable means beyond doubt.

questions.passage: The expedition's guide proved ______. She alone knew where water could be found, which passes were open, and how to bargain with the herders whose land the party had to cross.
questions.explanation: A guide whose knowledge the party could not manage without is essential.

distractors.why: Negligible means too unimportant to matter, the opposite of this guide.
Inadequate means not good enough, which she was not.
Untoward means unfortunate, which does not fit.

partsNote: not able to be weighed out and given away
